restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5: the 1600-bit permutation state is held in seven packed 256-bit registers P0..P6 (four 64-bit Keccak lanes per word, P6 holding A[24]); one five-round PERM5 call on them costs 1 unit; every other primitive costs 1/1355 units; jumps, moves, immediate 256-bit register writes and the call issue each cost one operation.
Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, prefix rounds 0 through 4, all 256 output bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x) = LE32(x).

Generic van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search on one processor: theta = 2^-32 via low-32-bits-zero on P0, maximum chain length 2^40, evaluation budget K0 = 65162*2^112, record cap 2^98, main loop unrolled 16 times; each evaluation rewrites P1..P6 with six 256-bit immediates, issues PERM5, and runs a 3-operation DP test; one run with no restart.

Time, memory and preprocessing are worst-case bounds for every run (time at most 2^128.00255, rounded up to 128.003). The success probability of at least 0.39 (exactly bounded below by 0.3900080 under H-RF) holds under the declared random-function heuristic H-RF.

Generic attack with no cryptanalytic improvement claimed; no stored collision, advice or precomputation. Published sub-birthday differential attacks on this target are not used. Tightens the prior 128.018 DP ticket by packing constant padding into six 256-bit restores instead of twenty-one lane-register writes.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x) = SHA3-256-r5(LE32(x)) on 256-bit words x: whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point it has not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of every value observed so far. This is the standard premise of the van Oorschot-Wiener analysis. It is used only to lower-bound the success probability (Section 6). Output correctness (Section 5) and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds (Sections 4, 7 and 8) are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: The fixed five-round prefix SHA3-256 restricted to 32-byte messages, iterated along pseudo-random chains from uniformly random 256-bit starts. The analysis uses only the chains started before the first contact (expected number below 2^96; at most 2^98 + 2^88 + 1 chains in any run) and at most K0 - 1 + 2^40 < 2^128 main-loop evaluations.
heuristics.extrapolation: We ran the Section 4 algorithm (with n-bit starts, a hash map in place of the trie and no record cap) on output-truncated versions of the real five-round map (n = 24, 32, 40 and 48 bits) and compared it with a keyed 24-round control. These tests are extrapolated to the full 256-bit map. The analytic success bound itself uses only the H-RF statement, not the measured numbers.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is false as a literal statement about a fixed deterministic function; it is a heuristic model, and five-round Keccak-f[1600] has known structured-input distinguishers and differential collision attacks, none of which a pseudo-random walk exercises. The supporting experiments are our own and are not organizer-executed (no experiment manifest is declared); their full source and exact arguments are in the proof. They cover only output widths of 24-48 bits on n-bit input subsets and cannot exclude a structural property that appears only at full width. The success bound exceeds 0.39 by only 8.0e-6; if H-RF overstated the contact probability by a small delta, restoring 0.39 would add about 2.4*delta bits to the scalar.
